title: The Fourth on the bay
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Fireworks over Alsea Bay from the uncle's dock. The only night with color. The strip can't afford color.

panels.composition: The dock at night, July. The UNCLE in a lawn chair with an oxygen line, small. GULLY and WOOD on the dock edge. BARNABY under the chair. Fireworks over the bay drawn in pure black and white: white bursts, black sky.

characters.pose: in a lawn chair with an oxygen line

image.prompt: a wooden dock at night with fireworks bursting white against a black sky over a bay, two young men on the dock edge, an old man in a lawn chair with an oxygen line, a small dog under the chair, high-contrast black and white
image.notes: The uncle's oxygen line: the first sign. Small. Not remarked.

balloons.text: This is the one night a year the strip should be in color.
So it's the one night a year you're wrong.

image.prompt: close-up of a young man looking up at fireworks beside a boy in a backwards cap, white light on their faces

panels.composition: The uncle, from the chair, not looking up.

image.prompt: close-up of an old man in a lawn chair with an oxygen line speaking without looking up at the fireworks

panels.composition: The finale. The bay. All white on black. The three of them and the dog, tiny. The only night the strip admits what it can't do.

image.prompt: a wide night panel of a fireworks finale over a bay rendered entirely in white bursts on black, a dock with three tiny figures and a dog, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The first Fourth. The uncle's oxygen line appears, unremarked. 'They were red in '71' — the 1971 wedding photo's dock.
